sentences.text: This animal possessed a body shape resembling a scaly ray with an upturned head. Its eyes and nostrils were positioned on top of its head, facing upward.
Instead of tooth plates, this animal used star-shaped scales to seize and swallow prey.
Specimens of Gemuendina stuertzi ranged from 30 to 100 centimeters in length.
Intact, nearly pristine specimens of Gemuendina were preserved in the anoxic Hunsruck lagerstätte.
The fragile armor of Gemuendina means few intact examples have survived in the fossil record.
The genus Gemuendina was named by Traquair in 1903, with Gemuendina stuertzi serving as the type species.
Broilina heroldi, described by Stensiö in 1971 as a one-meter long specimen, is now considered a synonym of Gemuendina.
Gemuendina is considered an example of convergent evolution due to its superficial similarity to rays. Its upturned mouth allowed it to suction prey swimming overhead, unlike modern rays.
Gemuendina is classified in the class Placodermi and belongs to the family Asterosteidae, which is its parent group.
Gemuendina stuertzi was a placoderm found in the seas of Early Devonian Germany during the Emsian stage, from 410.62 to 399.5 million years ago.
